svg.title: Clocking: two loops and two clock trees
svg.desc: Transmit side: refclk_buf feeds tx_pll, a loop of pfd, charge_pump (100 uA), loop_filter_rc (25.31 kilohm, 1.427 pF, plus C2 0.14 pF), vco and div_n (divide by 32), with lock_detect. Its 14 GHz output goes to tx_clkgen: dcc_cml, clkbuf_cml (clk14, CML), div2_cml (clk7, CML, an ideal placeholder), cml2cmos, phase_aligner (aligns to the retimed 7 Gb/s data), then three div2_tspc giving clk3p5, clk1p75 and clk0p875 (CMOS). Receive side: rx_cdr has one loop filter (2.352 kilohm, 20 pF, plus C2 1 pF) and one vco, and two detectors. First pfd and a 400 uA charge_pump lock the frequency to the reference; lock_detect or force_lock then turns that pump off, and cdr_pd_linear tracks the data from the analog front end against clk14. Its 14 GHz output goes to rx_clkgen: dcc_cml, clkbuf_cml (clk14, CML), two div2_cml placeholders (clk7 and clk3p5, CML), cml2cmos, then two div2_tspc giving clk1p75 and clk0p875 (CMOS).

g.text: Clocking: two loops and two clock trees
Each loop makes a 14 GHz clock from a 437.5 MHz reference. Each tree divides it down for the serializer or the deserializer.
tx_pll 437.5 MHz x 32 = 14 GHz. Type-II charge-pump loop, 21.875 MHz bandwidth.
ck: 14 GHz, single-ended CMOS (0 to 0.7 V)
rx_cdr one loop filter and one VCO, two detectors: frequency lock first, then the data.
ck: 14 GHz, single-ended CMOS (0 to 0.7 V)
CMOS on one side, CML on the other
